models.observations: A rounded manufacturing cell rises behind an open conveyor line with two articulated arms. Seen without paint, its working side and broad raised hood distinguish it from the Industrial long shed and stacks. The tall light roof sits on intact supports at LOD1.

A thick cantilever carries twin electrodes into an open glowing vessel. The clear gap beneath the beam distinguishes this foundry from the Industrial chimney furnace. The pier, cantilever, paired contacts and crucible all survive LOD1.

Two open dye vats and hanging cloth sit beneath a wide low eave. The Classical dye court replaces the Ancient hut and freestanding loom in the grey family views. Both columns, the workshop doorway and vat rims remain distinct at LOD1.

Thick end housings support a continuous roof over a large exposed red textile roll. The unpainted industrial loom has a pitched shed and external drive, both replaced here by an enclosed machine frame. LOD1 keeps the beam, end supports and roller gap.

A flue and geared wheel stand beside a sloping web of cloth feeding a wide roller. Its direction of work and roof line remain legible without colour. The wheel support, roller feet and workshop roof survive the middle level.

models.observations: The gap between the two stone bastions is visible from both approaches. The warm hipped caps and deep shield recesses give the frontage a recognizable armory entrance. At distance the shields simplify to framed panels while the gateway remains open.

The white battered end blocks carry their cyan caps cleanly at all three levels. Viewed without paint from either side, the two equal-height shield towers and low linking passage reproduce the Classical gate. The change to the roof caps barely affects the outline.
defects: Give the Future arsenal a different major volume or supported loading apparatus visible in both 64-pixel views. Retain that structural change at LOD2.

models.observations: The long brick works, end flue and continuous raised roof ridge replace the flanking gate towers. The shield racks and arched issue door read together from the front. The roof profile and chimney survive the rear and distant views.

The freestanding press frame and descending ram occupy the front of the boiler shed. A pipe bridges back toward the roof and the chimney rises behind it. The arch of the press and its plinth remain identifiable from front, flank and rear through LOD2.
